The autopkgtest regressions reported for systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8.19 have not been investigated or explained in any later comment. Several have concrete versions and so look like real failures, including netplan.io (amd64), dracut, initramfs-tools, apt, cron, exim4, libsoup3, munin, oomd, snapd and squid. The other "unknown" entries may be missing results. netplan.io is directly relevant to this networkd route change. SRU policy requires these to be triaged, or shown to be unrelated or flaky, before release.

The verification used a bonded host with a single default route and tested a networkd restart and a carrier drop. It did not run the documented test plan: the dummy-device netplan config with several routes in table 252, followed by `networkctl reconfigure` or `netplan apply`. It therefore did not confirm that exactly one route per entry, with the right MTUs (including the 9000 and link-scope routes), survives those steps. verification-done-noble was set on this evidence.

- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

excuses.status: BLOCKED: Rejected/violates migration policy/introduces a regression

findings.message: Either an Origin field or an Author/From field must be provided

blockers.summary: The bug does not say which Ubuntu series are affected or targeted. It also does not say whether the fix is already in the development release, which an SRU needs first. Only a debdiff and a PPA are mentioned, with no upload or merge evidence.
The test plan verifies the fix by hand-editing /etc/apparmor.d/linux-boot-prober. It never installs the updated apparmor package from -proposed, so the packaged profile is not actually tested.

The 'Other Info' section says that fixing this exposes a separate os-prober defect with LVM snapshots (LP #1987679 and LP #2155998), which the AppArmor denial currently masks. After the SRU, users with LVM snapshots could see bogus or duplicate GRUB entries. The 'Where problems could occur' section does not cover this, and the fix is tracked separately.
